items.stem: What distinguishes kernel mode from user mode?

options.text: Kernel mode can execute privileged instructions and access hardware directly; user mode cannot
options.rationale: Correct: the privilege separation protects the system; user code must request services via system calls.

options.text: User mode is faster because it skips all checks
options.rationale: User mode is restricted, not a performance tier; privilege is the distinction.

options.text: Kernel mode runs only at boot
options.rationale: The kernel runs throughout operation whenever privileged work is needed.

options.text: They differ only in which language the code is written in
options.rationale: The distinction is privilege level, not programming language.

items.explanation: Correct: the privilege separation protects the system; user code must request services via system calls.

items.stem: Which statements about threads versus processes are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Threads within a process share the same address space
options.rationale: Correct: threads share code, heap and globals, which is why synchronisation matters.

options.text: Creating a thread is generally cheaper than creating a process
options.rationale: Correct: threads avoid duplicating the full address space, so they are lighter weight.

options.text: Each thread has its own completely separate address space
options.rationale: Separate address spaces belong to processes, not threads of one process.

options.text: Processes always share memory by default
options.rationale: Processes are isolated by default; sharing requires explicit mechanisms.

items.explanation: Correct: threads share code, heap and globals, which is why synchronisation matters.; Correct: threads avoid duplicating the full address space, so they are lighter weight.

items.stem: Which set of conditions must all hold for a deadlock to be possible?

options.text: Mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, and circular wait
options.rationale: Correct: these four Coffman conditions must all hold simultaneously for deadlock.
Mutual exclusion alone does not cause deadlock; all four conditions are needed.

options.text: High CPU utilisation and low memory
options.rationale: Resource pressure is not the formal condition for deadlock.

options.text: A single process using a single resource
options.rationale: Deadlock requires a circular wait among multiple processes/resources.

items.explanation: Correct: these four Coffman conditions must all hold simultaneously for deadlock.
